title: Cascade Analytics kickstart workshop & POC acceptance
content:
Context:
Cascade Analytics is evaluating Redwood for a customer-facing insights assistant that runs on customer data streams (clicks, event logs, user notes). They want a 6-week pilot to validate latency, cost, and extraction quality before a larger Dedicated commitment. This doc captures kickoff notes, workshop agenda, measurable success criteria, and acceptance tests.

High-level goals (customer-facing):
- Demonstrate reliable inference at production-like load on Redwood Hosted with optional Dedicated trial window.
- Prove extraction quality for three vertical intents (billing, feature-usage, churn signals) with baseline F1 targets.
- Show cost and latency forecasts for 100k monthly active users (MAU) workload.

Primary contacts:
- Cascade: Priya Nair (PM), Tomas Vega (Platform eng), Luke Anders (Data eng)
- Redwood: Noah Patel (Solutions Eng, owner), Maya Reynolds (SWE), Eric Zhou (SRE lead)

Kickoff workshop objectives (90m):
1) Alignment: scope, success metrics, roles, non-goals (15m)
2) Data reality check: sample records, PII surface, residency constraints (20m)
3) Integration plan: ingestion methods (push vs pull), auth, network (20m)
4) Eval design: labels, test harness, metrics, initial eval pass (20m)
5) Next steps & immediate actions (15m)

Proposed agenda (detailed):
- 0:00–0:05 quick intros + what success looks like (Priya / Noah)
- 0:05–0:20 Data walk-through: show 5 anonymized rows, schema mapping, note missing values (Luke)
- 0:20–0:40 Architecture options: hosted API with VPC peering vs Dedicated trial; tradeoffs on latency and data isolation (Maya)
- 0:40–1:00 Eval plan + labeling rubric: who labels, sampling, edge cases, and where to store labels (Eric)
- 1:00–1:15 Deployment ramp & rollback plan; SLOs + alerts (Noah)
- 1:15–1:30 Action items, owners, timeline (all)

Success criteria (must pass all for POC sign-off):
1) Quality: intent extraction F1 >= 0.88 for each of the three target intents on a 2k-sample holdout set (evaluation script in repo).
2) Latency: p95 end-to-end inference latency < 150 ms for 512-token typical sequence at steady state (burstable to 250 ms allowed for cold-starts).
3) Throughput: system sustains 300 qps for 10 minutes with <2% error rate in the Hosted config; Dedicated trial should sustain 1k qps baseline.
4) Cost forecast: projected cost per 1k users for inference and caching configurations <= agreed budget of $1.20 per 1k MAU (model + infra).
5) Security & compliance: data path uses VPC peering and encryption-at-rest, no PII persisted in Redwood index; SOC2 controls checklist signed.
6) Observability: console shows token-level cost breakdown and per-request trace for at least 72h of pilot traffic.

Acceptance tests / runbook (concrete):
- Baseline eval: run eval/baseline_eval.py against holdout.csv -> produces per-intent precision/recall/F1.
- Load test: run loadtest/k6-script.json against hosted endpoint with 300 qps for 10m; aggregate p95, error rate.
- Latency microbenchmark: single-client 256/512/1024 token traces recorded; confirm p50/p95/p99.
- Failover test: simulate model-instance OOM and verify fallback to smaller compatible variant within 10s without request loss.
- Security check: KMS logs + VPC route verification step-by-step.

Deliverables (by end of week 2):
- Ingestion recipe & sample connector (S3 -> Redwood streaming ingest), documented in README.
- Labeling spreadsheet with 2k rows and labeling guide (shared with Cascade data team).
- Baseline eval report (notebook + summary slide) with per-intent metrics and confusion examples.
- Cost model spreadsheet (simple calc for hosted vs dedicated) with sensitivity knobs (batch size, kv cache hit rate).

Timeline (6-week pilot):
- Week 0 (kickoff): workshop + data access + Atlassian ticket intake
- Week 1: ingestion connector + first 200 labeled rows; initial hosted smoke test
- Week 2: baseline eval pass, load test config, begin Dedicated sizing conversations if needed
- Week 3: optimize batching & KV caching; update cost model; iterate on prompts and eval
- Week 4: 72h production-like run, observability review, SLO tuning
- Week 5: sign-off readiness checklist, compliance artifacts collected
- Week 6: decision milestone (go/no-go to Dedicated / wider rollout)

Open questions / risks (to resolve during or immediately after workshop):
- Data freshness SLA: Cascade wants <5s ingestion; hosted streaming ingestion currently target ~10s. Can we meet <5s with current connectors? (action: Maya to experiment by 2025-09-22).
- Residency: Cascade requires EU-only data residency for logs. Confirm Hosted EU region supports retention/processing without US egress. (action: Eric follow-up).
- Labeling resources: Cascade will provide 2 contract annotators but might need Redwood labeling for edge-case hunting. Budget approval pending.

Quick notes to self (choppy / TODOs):
- Bring small demo payloads: billing_event.json, usage_event.json
- Prep cost baseline slide: two scenarios (KV cache 20% vs 60% hit)
- Add sample alert thresholds to the runbook (p95>200ms -> page oncall)
- Slack thread: #poc-cascade for asynchronous Qs; pin workshop artifacts

Post-workshop immediate actions (owners):
- Noah: Create repo skeleton + eval script template (due 48h)
- Luke (Cascade): Share sanitized sample dataset (due 72h)
- Maya: Prototype ingestion lambda and S3 connector (due 5 working days)
- Eric: Draft SLOs + alerting playbook and confirm EU region hosting constraints (due 5 working days)

Appendix: quick measurement notes and heuristics
- Suggest using Redwood Optimize profiles: batch_size=8, kv_cache_enabled=true for event-extraction workloads with repetitive prefixes; expected cost delta -15% at 40% cache hit.
- For privacy, run masking at ingress: token removal for 3 fields (email, device_id, ssn-like patterns).

End-state for sign-off: Cascade has a reproducible eval notebook, 72-hour production-like trace in Redwood Console showing SLOs met, and a signed acceptance note from Priya. If any single acceptance criterion fails, iterate for two weeks; second review gates final decision.

References & links (for workshop):
- Internal playbook: CONFLUENCE-4567 (POC runbook)
- Cost calc template: github.com/redwood-inference/cost-templates/poc-cost-model.xlsx
- Incident runbook stub: github.com/redwood-inference/runbooks/poc-fallback.md
